candidates.summary: Each unclosed inline `$` opener scans the whole rest of its line and the next line for a closer, so a line of openers renders in quadratic time: 1 MiB takes ~57-60 s per page view, against 40 ms at the merge base
candidates.failure_scenario: A realm's Render returns one 1 MiB line of `$a ` (349,525 openers, which fits under gnoweb's 1 MiB maxMarkdownRenderBytes). findDollarClose skips every `$` that follows a space, so each opener walks to the end of the line and then through the next line. Each page view costs about 57-60 s of gnoweb CPU, and a few concurrent requests occupy every core. The merge base renders the same input in 40.5 ms. Unclosed `\\(a ` openers grow 4x per doubling too (they use bytes.Index). The 1 MiB cap was set because ~8 s was already too much.
candidates.verify_by: cp tests/solo-finder-2-inline-dollar-quadratic.go gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/markdown/zz_quad_repro_test.go && go test -v -count=1 -timeout 600s -run TestInlineDollarQuadratic ./gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/markdown/ at 0193f6de7 and at 87f0357fe: time grows 4x per doubling at head, linearly at base

candidates.summary: The 8 KiB cap bounds one expression but not a page. Aligned `&` cells render at 107x, which breaks the PR's own FuzzMathRender bound (64x+4096), and a 1 MiB page renders to 112 MB of HTML
candidates.failure_scenario: A realm returns 1 MiB of markdown made of 128 `$\begin{aligned}&&&...\end{aligned}$` expressions, each under 8 KiB. Every `&` emits an <mtd> carrying text-align and padding CSS at a 32-space indent (environnements.go:227-234). One render produces 111,811,584 bytes of HTML and allocates about 2.5 GB in 1.4 s. The worst existing non-math shape at the same 1 MiB is nested blockquotes: 28 MB of output and 225 MB of allocation. With the input as a corpus entry, FuzzMathRender fails with 'output too large: 872458 bytes for 8180 bytes of input', so the 'output size stays linear' bound the fuzz header states does not hold.
candidates.verify_by: cp tests/solo-finder-2-page-amplification.go gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/markdown/zz_amp_repro_test.go && go test -v -run TestPageAmplification ./gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/markdown/; then add the aligned corpus file from the header and run go test -run FuzzMathRender ./gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/markdown/ (expect FAIL at ext_math_test.go:137)

candidates.summary: The block lookahead accepts any later line containing `$$` within 8 KiB, past blank lines, headings and code fences. A stray `$$` line therefore still swallows everything up to a later inline `$$x$$` and renders it as math identifiers
candidates.failure_scenario:
In a board or comment realm, one post contains a line that is only `$$`. A later post within 8 KiB uses `$$x$$` inline. hasClosingLine finds that line, the block opens, and Continue appends every line in between, blank lines included. The other posts' headings, paragraphs and fenced code then render as one of letters with a `?#` merror, and the tail after the inline `$$` is left as a stray `

x$$ display.

`. Without the later `$$` the same input renders correctly, so the round-1 fix only closed the never-closed case. Pandoc ends `$$` math at a blank line.
